title: Seek the LORD
backstory: Zephaniah preached in Judah in the days of young King Josiah, when idols still lurked on rooftops and in secret corners of the land. His book traces his family line back four generations to a man named Hizkiah, whom many believe was Judah's good King Hezekiah, and God gave him an urgent message: the great day of the LORD is near. Yet inside the warning is a door of hope, held open for everyone humble enough to seek the LORD.

passages.synopsis: The word of the LORD came to Zephaniah in the days of King Josiah of Judah. The warning begins as wide as the world: God says He will utterly consume all things from off the land, man and beast, the fowls of the heaven and the fishes of the sea. Then it narrows to Judah and Jerusalem, where He would cut off every trace of Baal and everyone who bowed to the host of heaven on their housetops. Some people had turned back from the LORD and had not sought Him at all. Then comes a call to hush: hold thy peace at the presence of the Lord GOD, for the day of the LORD is at hand.

Zephaniah says the great day of the LORD is near — near, and hasting greatly. He piles up words to describe it: a day of wrath, a day of trouble and distress, a day of wasteness and desolation. It is a day of darkness and gloominess, a day of clouds and thick darkness. It is a day of the trumpet and the alarm sounding against the fenced cities and the high towers. The warning is meant to wake people up while there is still time to turn back to God.

Then Zephaniah names the one thing his people trusted most, and shows how little it could do. Neither their silver nor their gold would be able to deliver them in the day of the LORD's wrath. The whole land would be devoured by the fire of His jealousy. Riches cannot buy safety from God, and the prophet says so plainly so that his hearers will stop trusting their treasure and start seeking the LORD.

Zephaniah pleads with the nation to gather together before the day arrives, before it passes like chaff blown from the threshing floor. Then comes the heart of his message: seek ye the LORD, all ye meek of the earth. Seek righteousness and seek meekness. It may be that the humble will be hid — kept safe by God himself — in the day of the LORD's anger.

triviaQuestions.question: To which prophet did the word of the LORD come in this book?
triviaQuestions.explanation: Zephaniah 1:1 — "The word of the LORD which came unto Zephaniah the son of Cushi, the son of Gedaliah, the son of Amariah, the son of Hizkiah, in the days of Josiah the son of Amon, king of Judah."

triviaQuestions.question: What did Zephaniah say was at hand?
triviaQuestions.explanation: Zephaniah 1:7 — "Hold thy peace at the presence of the Lord GOD: for the day of the LORD is at hand: for the LORD hath prepared a sacrifice, he hath bid his guests."

triviaQuestions.question: What three things did Zephaniah tell the meek of the earth to seek?
triviaQuestions.explanation: Zephaniah 2:3 — "Seek ye the LORD, all ye meek of the earth, which have wrought his judgment; seek righteousness, seek meekness: it may be ye shall be hid in the day of the LORD’s anger."

triviaQuestions.question: Zephaniah said the day would pass like what?
triviaQuestions.explanation: Zephaniah 2:2 — "Before the decree bring forth, before the day pass as the chaff, before the fierce anger of the LORD come upon you, before the day of the LORD’s anger come upon you."

whoAmIChars.name: Zephaniah
clues: The word of the LORD came to me in the days of King Josiah.
My book traces my family back four generations, through Cushi, Gedaliah, and Amariah, to Hizkiah.
I warned that the great day of the LORD was near, and told the meek to seek the LORD.

whoAmIChars.name: Josiah
clues: I was king of Judah when Zephaniah preached.
My father was Amon, but I did not follow his ways.
I did what was right in the sight of the LORD and led my people back to him.

reflection: Zephaniah says the humble who seek the LORD may be hid — kept safe — in the day of trouble. What would it look like for you to seek the LORD, righteousness, and meekness this week?
